away.

been picked up once.

do not open.

on willpower.

distracting apps close with it.

does, not when I give in.

for exactly that block.

Screen with the time left on it.

block that protects it.

My holy grail.
Every task has a time and the block
that protects it is the same app.
I stopped running a planner and a
blocker that knew nothing about
each other.
One app, one day.
I plan the whole day before I start
it, so nothing waits on a decision.
I get more done by noon than I used
to manage by six.
The plan does the deciding.
Blocked Hours shuts my apps from
six to eight, every evening.
I set it once and my screen time is
down by half.
I never argue with it.
Every time I open TikTok the shield
comes up instead of the feed.
The reflex still happens, it just
turns into a reminder to lock in.
That is the whole app.
Every task I have sits on one page
with a time next to it.
I stopped keeping half the list in
my head and losing the other half.
One page, the whole day.
One button starts the block and
locks every app on the list.
No settings and no deciding, I am
in and the phone is out.
One tap and I am working.
Insights shows the week by app and
by day, in hours.
Seeing four hours on one app is what
made me finally cut it.
The number did the convincing.
Habits take a real slot on the day,
the same as any task.
Mine lasted past the first month
because the day made room for it.
That is why they finally stuck.
The block I am in sits on the Lock
Screen with the time left running.
I pick the phone up and it tells me
to get back to work.
My holy grail.
Tasks with no time wait in Anytime
instead of crowding today.
Today holds only what I gave an
hour to, so I actually finish it.
The list stopped lying to me.
Focus mode puts every distracting
app away for the whole session.
An hour of work is an hour now, not
forty minutes and a scroll.
I get the time back.

rule: Pick by THEME so the slide answers the hook -- hook_pool.json carries the theme and _tools_photo enforces it.
